children: Iron ore prices slid for a second straight session on Thursday to hit their lowest in nearly a week, dragged down by concerns over falling demand in top consumer China as steel margins continued to deteriorate.
The benchmark October iron ore (SZZFV6) on the Singapore Exchange was 0.31% lower at $99.15 a metric ton, as of 0124 GMT after touching its lowest since September 4 at $98.95.
The contract stood above a key psychological level of $100 for four sessions, supported by rising freight costs caused by elevated energy prices.
The most-traded iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
slipped 0.81% to 731.5 yuan a ton, as of 0134 GMT, its weakest since September 7.
"Hot metal output is expected to fall as losses widened among steelmakers following the latest rise in spot coke prices," said analysts at broker Everbright Futures in a note.
Hot metal is a blast furnace product, and its output is typically used to gauge iron ore demand.
Around 30% of steelmakers were operating at a profit as of September 4, versus 32.5% the week before and 61% over the same period in the prior year, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.
